data.mechanism: LKB1 is the main kinase that primes AMPK, phosphorylating AMPK-alpha directly on Thr172; in LKB1-null cells AMPK no longer responds to energy stress (SHW2004). It is not the only upstream kinase: CaMKK2 phosphorylates the same site when calcium rises, and LKB1-deficient cells keep some basal AMPK activity (Hawley 2005, PMID 16054095; Woods 2005, PMID 16054096; outside this corpus).
data.mechanism_beginner: LKB1 is the main switch that turns AMPK on when energy runs low; in cells without it, AMPK no longer responds to low energy. A second kinase can still switch AMPK on when calcium rises, so AMPK is not completely silent.
data.boundary: Canonical step, established in LKB1-null cells and in vitro kinase assays (SHW2004). Coded M – molecular – because that is what the supporting evidence is: cell and in vitro biochemistry, not an organismal phenotype.
data.note: 2026-10-10: 'without it the whole energy-stress arm is deaf' / 'the whole alarm system goes silent' narrowed. LKB1 loss removes the response to energy stress, not all AMPK activity (CaMKK2 arm, Hawley 2005 / Woods 2005).
